answer.summary: For Truell, developing a “taste” means building a practical sense of what a model can handle, where it falls short, and how much guidance it needs—through iterative use and safe experimentation. Models have different quirks, so that sense may need updating as models change.

sections.heading: What “taste” means
sections.content: It is knowing what complexity of task a model can handle, how specifically you need to instruct it, and the model’s quality, strengths, and gaps—what it can and cannot do.

sections.heading: How to develop it
sections.content: Rather than give the model one giant prompt for a large task and accept or reject the whole result, break the work into smaller pieces: specify a bit, get some work, then specify the next bit. To discover the model’s limits, Truell also recommends trying ambitious uses in a safe setting, such as a side project, and being willing to fail; people may otherwise underestimate what the model can do. Different models have different quirks and personalities, so your sense of their capabilities may need to be refreshed when models change.
